source.statute_ref: Tex. Const. art. VIII, § 24 (voter-approved 2019 ban on a state personal income tax)

steps: Start with your gross annual salary.
Subtract the 2026 federal standard deduction ($16,100 single) to get taxable income, then apply the 2026 federal brackets (10%-37%).
Subtract FICA: 6.2% Social Security (up to the $184,500 wage base) + 1.45% Medicare (all wages, +0.9% above $200,000).
Texas charges no state income tax — your paycheck stops there. What's left is your net take-home pay.

example.scenario: Example: $65,000/year gross salary, single filer, Texas resident.

faq_extra.q: Does Texas have a state income tax?
faq_extra.a: No. Texas is one of nine states with no personal income tax, a status enshrined in the Texas Constitution since a 2019 voter-approved amendment (art. VIII, § 24). Your paycheck only has federal income tax and FICA withheld.

faq_extra.q: How much is take-home pay on $65,000 in Texas?
faq_extra.a: On a $65,000 gross salary, a single filer in Texas takes home roughly $54,440/year (about $4,537/month) after federal income tax and FICA — no state tax is withheld.

faq_extra.q: Are there any hidden state or local income taxes in Texas?
faq_extra.a: No Texas city or county levies a local income tax. Texas instead relies more heavily on sales tax and property tax to fund state and local government.

source.statute_ref: 72 P.S. § 7302 — flat 3.07% Personal Income Tax rate, unchanged since 2004

steps: Start with your gross annual salary.
Subtract the 2026 federal standard deduction ($16,100 single), apply the 2026 federal brackets (10%-37%).
Subtract FICA: 6.2% Social Security (up to $184,500) + 1.45% Medicare (+0.9% above $200,000).
Subtract Pennsylvania's flat 3.07% state tax — applied to gross wages, with no standard deduction or personal exemption.
What's left is your net take-home pay before any local Earned Income Tax (EIT).

example.scenario: Example: $65,000/year gross salary, single filer, Pennsylvania resident.

faq_extra.q: What is Pennsylvania's state income tax rate?
faq_extra.a: Pennsylvania charges a flat 3.07% Personal Income Tax on gross wages, a rate that has not changed since 2004. There is no standard deduction or personal exemption.

faq_extra.q: Does this calculator include Philadelphia or other local wage taxes?
faq_extra.a: No. This estimate covers only the state's 3.07% flat tax. Pennsylvania municipalities and school districts levy an additional local Earned Income Tax (EIT), commonly 1%-3.9%+, with Philadelphia at the high end. Check your municipality's EIT rate separately.

faq_extra.q: How much is take-home pay on $65,000 in Pennsylvania?
faq_extra.a: On a $65,000 gross salary, a single filer in Pennsylvania takes home roughly $52,444/year (about $4,370/month) after federal tax, FICA, and the state's 3.07% flat tax — before any local EIT.

source.statute_ref: 35 ILCS 5/201 — flat 4.95% rate (Illinois Constitution art. IX, § 3 prohibits graduated rates)

steps: Start with your gross annual salary.
Subtract the 2026 federal standard deduction ($16,100 single), apply the 2026 federal brackets (10%-37%).
Subtract FICA: 6.2% Social Security (up to $184,500) + 1.45% Medicare (+0.9% above $200,000).
Subtract Illinois's $2,425 personal exemption from gross wages, then apply the flat 4.95% state rate to the remainder.
What's left is your net take-home pay — Illinois has no local income tax.

example.scenario: Example: $65,000/year gross salary, single filer, Illinois resident.

faq_extra.q: What is Illinois's state income tax rate?
faq_extra.a: Illinois charges a flat 4.95% income tax rate on all taxable income — the Illinois Constitution (art. IX, § 3) prohibits graduated rates. Each filer gets a $2,425 personal exemption in 2026.

faq_extra.q: Does Illinois tax retirement income?
faq_extra.a: No — Illinois does not tax Social Security, pension income, or 401(k)/IRA withdrawals, making it comparatively favorable for retirees despite the flat wage tax.

faq_extra.q: Does Illinois have local income tax?
faq_extra.a: No. Unlike Pennsylvania or Ohio, no Illinois city or county adds a separate local income tax on top of the state's flat 4.95% rate.

steps: Start with your gross annual salary.

example.scenario: Example: $65,000/year gross salary, single filer, Georgia resident.

faq_extra.q: What is Georgia's state income tax rate in 2026?
faq_extra.a: Georgia charges a flat 4.99% rate for tax year 2026, cut from 5.19% by HB 463 (signed May 11, 2026, retroactive to January 1, 2026). The law schedules further 0.125%-point annual cuts starting 2027 until the rate reaches 3.99%.

faq_extra.q: What is Georgia's standard deduction?
faq_extra.a: $15,000 for single filers and married filing separately in 2026 (up from prior years under HB 463), $30,000 for married filing jointly.

faq_extra.q: Does Georgia have local income tax?
faq_extra.a: No. Georgia counties and cities do not levy separate local income taxes on wages.

faq_extra.q: Is North Carolina's income tax rate still dropping?
faq_extra.a: Yes. Under Session Law 2023-134, North Carolina's flat rate has phased down annually — 4.5% (2024), 4.25% (2025), 3.99% (2026) — with further cuts to 3.75% (2027) and 3.5% (2028) scheduled if state revenue triggers are met.

faq_extra.q: What is North Carolina's standard deduction for 2026?
faq_extra.a: $12,750 for single filers under current law. A pending bill (S437) would raise it to $13,000, but that had not been enacted as of this page's last-verified date — check ncdor.gov for the final figure.

faq_extra.q: Does North Carolina have local income tax?
faq_extra.a: No. North Carolina counties and municipalities do not levy separate local income taxes on wages.

source.statute_ref: Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code § 17041 — 9-bracket schedule (1%-12.3%) plus 1% Mental Health Services Tax on taxable income over $1,000,000 (top effective rate 13.3%)

steps: Start with your gross annual salary.
Subtract the 2026 federal standard deduction ($16,100 single), apply the 2026 federal brackets (10%-37%).
Subtract FICA: 6.2% Social Security (up to $184,500) + 1.45% Medicare (+0.9% above $200,000).
Subtract California's $5,706 standard deduction from gross wages, then apply the 9-bracket state schedule (1%-12.3%) marginally — plus 1% Mental Health Services Tax on income over $1,000,000.
Subtract California SDI (1.3% of all wages, no cap in 2026) — a mandatory payroll deduction, not an income tax, but it reduces your paycheck.
What's left is your net take-home pay.

example.scenario: Example: $65,000/year gross salary, single filer, California resident.
calculation: CA taxable income: $65,000 - $5,706 = $59,294 → marginal CA tax = $2,203.76

faq_extra.q: What are California's income tax brackets for 2026?
faq_extra.a: California uses 9 marginal brackets from 1% (income up to $10,756) to 12.3% (over $721,314 for single filers), plus a 1% Mental Health Services Tax on taxable income over $1,000,000, for a 13.3% top effective rate.

faq_extra.q: What is California SDI and is it a tax?
faq_extra.a: State Disability Insurance (SDI) is a mandatory payroll deduction, not a state income tax — 1.3% of all wages in 2026 with no wage cap. It funds short-term disability and Paid Family Leave benefits and is withheld separately from income tax.

faq_extra.q: How much is take-home pay on $65,000 in California?
faq_extra.a: On a $65,000 gross salary, a single filer in California takes home roughly $50,942/year (about $4,245/month) after federal tax, FICA, state income tax, and SDI.

source.statute_ref: N.Y. Tax Law § 601 — FY2026 budget cut the bottom five bracket rates 0.1 point starting tax year 2026

steps: Start with your gross annual salary.
Subtract the 2026 federal standard deduction ($16,100 single), apply the 2026 federal brackets (10%-37%).
Subtract FICA: 6.2% Social Security (up to $184,500) + 1.45% Medicare (+0.9% above $200,000).
Subtract New York's $8,000 standard deduction from gross wages, then apply the 9-bracket state schedule (4%-10.9%) marginally.
Subtract New York Paid Family Leave (0.432% of wages, capped at $411.91/year in 2026) — a mandatory payroll deduction, not income tax.
What's left is your net take-home pay before any New York City or Yonkers resident tax.

example.scenario: Example: $65,000/year gross salary, single filer, New York State resident (outside NYC).
calculation: NY taxable income: $65,000 - $8,000 = $57,000 → marginal NY tax ≈ $2,904.35

faq_extra.q: What are New York's state income tax brackets for 2026?
faq_extra.a: New York has 9 brackets for single filers, from 4% on income up to $17,150 to 10.9% above $25,000,000. The FY2026 budget cut the bottom five bracket rates by 0.1 point.

faq_extra.q: Does this calculator include New York City tax?
faq_extra.a: No. This estimate covers only New York State tax. NYC residents owe an additional local income tax (3.078%-3.876%), and Yonkers residents owe a local surcharge — neither is computed here.

faq_extra.q: What is New York Paid Family Leave (PFL)?
faq_extra.a: A mandatory employee payroll deduction — 0.432% of wages in 2026, capped at $411.91/year — that funds paid leave benefits. It is separate from income tax.

source.statute_ref: Ohio Rev. Code § 5747.02 — completion of the multi-year phase-down to a single 2.75% bracket for 2026 (3.5% in 2024, 3.125% in 2025, 2.75% in 2026), with the first $26,050 of nonbusiness income untaxed

steps: Start with your gross annual salary.
Subtract the 2026 federal standard deduction ($16,100 single), apply the 2026 federal brackets (10%-37%).
Subtract FICA: 6.2% Social Security (up to $184,500) + 1.45% Medicare (+0.9% above $200,000).
Ohio taxes the first $26,050 of income at 0%, then a flat 2.75% on everything above that — no separate standard deduction to subtract first.
What's left is your net take-home pay before any municipal income tax.

example.scenario: Example: $65,000/year gross salary, single filer, Ohio resident.

faq_extra.q: What is Ohio's state income tax rate in 2026?
faq_extra.a: Ohio completed a multi-year phase-down to a single flat rate for 2026: 0% on the first $26,050 of nonbusiness income, then 2.75% on everything above that — down from 3.125% in 2025 and 3.5% in 2024.

faq_extra.q: Does this calculator include Ohio city/municipal income tax?
faq_extra.a: No — and this matters a lot in Ohio. Over 600 Ohio municipalities levy their own income tax, typically 1%-3%, with Columbus, Cleveland, and Akron around 2.5%. For many Ohio taxpayers, city tax exceeds state tax. Check your city's rate at your municipality's finance department or RITA/CCA (Ohio's two major municipal tax collection agencies) — it is not included in this estimate.

faq_extra.q: How much is take-home pay on $65,000 in Ohio?
faq_extra.a: On a $65,000 gross salary, a single filer in Ohio takes home roughly $53,368/year (about $4,447/month) after federal tax, FICA, and Ohio's 2.75% state tax — before any city income tax, which can add another 1%-3%.
